original_title: GTA's treatment of women 'has not been good', says Rockstar vet delighted by 'long overdue' female protagonist in GTA 6
summary_en: A founding voice behind the original Grand Theft Auto is speaking out about the series' historical treatment of women. He expresses significant delight over the upcoming GTA 6 featuring a Latina protagonist.
ai_analysis: This piece delves into the historical context of female representation in the Grand Theft Auto series, a topic of keen interest to long-time fans and newcomers alike, as GTA 6's Lucia promises a significant shift.

en.title: GTA Veteran Calls Series' Female Portrayal 'Not Good,' Praises GTA 6's Lucia
en.summary: A founding voice behind the original Grand Theft Auto is speaking out about the series' historical treatment of women. He expresses significant delight over the upcoming GTA 6 featuring a Latina protagonist.
en.body:
For decades, the **Grand Theft Auto** series has been a cultural behemoth, pushing boundaries and sparking conversations with its satirical take on crime and society. Yet, a critical look back reveals a persistent blind spot: the portrayal of women. Now, a veteran from the series' early days is highlighting this issue and celebrating a long-overdue change.

**Brian Baglow**, who served as a writer on the original **GTA** and held the unique title of "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would evolve into Rockstar North), has spoken candidly about the franchise's past. He acknowledges that while the original **GTA** and **GTA 2** featured playable female characters, their presence in the modern, globally dominant era of the series has been notably absent until now. Baglow's perspective comes from the ground floor, where the original game was famously developed with a tech demo and a rapidly evolving script. "We were making it up as we went along," Baglow recalled, describing a process of drawing inspiration from a vast array of crime films, heist stories, and cop dramas. This improvisational approach, while leading to a groundbreaking title, apparently left little room for nuanced character development, particularly for female roles.

## Acknowledging Past Shortcomings

Reflecting on his foundational work, Baglow expressed pride but did not shy away from criticism. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly," he stated. This frank assessment sets the stage for his enthusiasm regarding **GTA 6**'s lead, Lucia. He views her as not just a female protagonist, but a *Hispanic* female protagonist, a detail he finds particularly significant. "I think it's been long, long overdue," Baglow commented, conveying his eagerness to experience the game and explore the depth of Lucia's character. This sentiment suggests a hope that **Rockstar Games** is finally addressing a long-standing imbalance within its flagship franchise, aligning with the evolving expectations of a global audience.

## Fan Anticipation for a New Era

The reveal of Lucia as **GTA 6**'s co-protagonist alongside **Lucia** has already generated significant buzz among fans. For many, the opportunity to play as a female lead in the series' current, highly polished iteration represents a significant and welcome evolution. Community discussions often touch upon the desire for more diverse protagonists, and Lucia's introduction is seen by many as a positive step towards greater inclusivity. The anticipation is palpable, with players eager to see how this new perspective will shape the narrative and gameplay experience, moving beyond the series' historically male-dominated focus. It’s a change many in the community feel is not just overdue, but essential for the franchise's continued relevance.

## What's Next for Vice City

While **GTA 6**'s release date remains a subject of intense speculation, with publisher **Take-Two Interactive** having previously signaled a tendency for delays, the anticipation for its debut continues to build. Fans are eagerly awaiting further details on gameplay, story, and any potential glimpses into Lucia's character arc. The game is expected to launch sometime in 2025.

content_raw: Lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed. That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens , GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue". Baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built". That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people". Baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an important series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist. I think it's been long, long overdue, and I can't wait to get to grips with the game and see how in-depth it goes. "I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland".
